question: From what date can private tenants in England no longer be evicted using a 'no fault' Section 21 notice under the Renters' Rights Act?
answer:
Private tenants in England can no longer be evicted using a Section 21 "no fault" notice from 1 May 2026 [1][2][7]. The Renters' Rights Act 2025 (Commencement No. 2 and Transitional and Saving Provisions) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/421) brought Chapter 1 of Part 1 of the Act into force on that date for private assured tenancies, abolishing fixed-term and shorthold assured tenancies and "section 21 evictions" [1]. A GOV.UK release of 30 April 2026 confirms the ban is in force from 1 May 2026 [7], and a Housing Hub page dated October 2026 says Section 21 has been abolished [4].

There is a transitional exception for Section 21 claims already in the court process [2][7]. Section 21 possession claims already going through the courts on the commencement date proceed as normal [2]. If a landlord served a Section 21 notice before 1 May 2026, court proceedings must be brought under the usual rules and no later than 31 July 2026 [7].

This covers England only, and the rules differ elsewhere in the UK. This is general legal information, not legal advice. A specific situation needs a licensed lawyer.

keyPoints.text: Section 21 'no-fault' evictions were abolished for private tenancies in England from 1 May 2026.
The commencement regulations bringing Chapter 1 of Part 1 into force on 1 May 2026 were made on 16 April 2026.
Section 21 possession claims already in court before 1 May 2026 continue, and must be brought no later than 31 July 2026 where a Section 21 notice was served before that date.
Government announced the 1 May 2026 date in a press release on 13 November 2025.
